claims.text: In a single-phase HEA superconductor, superconducting transition temperature is governed primarily by average valence electron concentration per atom.
Valence electron concentration controls the electronic density of states at the Fermi level.
The electronic density of states at the Fermi level controls electron-phonon coupling strength.
Equiatomic Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.2 is a single-phase HEA.
Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.2 has an average VEC of approximately 4.8.
Replacing 10 at.% Zr with 10 at.% Ti raises the average VEC.
Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.1Ti0.1 has an average VEC of approximately 4.9.
The Ti-for-Zr substitution can retain a single-phase solid solution.
Ti substitution slightly contracts the lattice parameter.
A higher VEC raises the electronic density of states at the Fermi level in this alloy.
The increased density of states enhances the electron-phonon coupling constant λ.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling produces a higher superconducting transition temperature.
The Ti-substituted alloy will have a transition temperature approximately 0.3–0.7 K above that of the baseline alloy.
The proposed VEC relationship applies only to single-phase disordered solid solutions without significant chemical ordering or second-phase formation and for VEC changes no greater than 0.2.
The electronic specific-heat coefficient γ should increase in proportion to VEC.
Failure of the substituted alloy's transition temperature to increase by more than ±0.2 K, or failure of γ to follow VEC, is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The stated VEC values are inconsistent with the listed compositions under conventional transition-metal VEC counting: Re0.2Mo0.2W0.2Ta0.2Zr0.2 gives about 5.6 rather than 4.8, and replacing Zr with same-group Ti leaves the average VEC unchanged rather than raising it to 4.9.

The proposed intervention does not create the claimed higher-electron-count mediator because Ti and Zr have the same conventional valence count. Consequently, attributing changes in density of states, λ, T_c, or γ to an increase in VEC is internally incoherent, and the proposed γ-versus-VEC falsification test has no actual VEC contrast.
